statement: Two distinct non-opposite rays $OA$ and $OB$ share origin $O$. Can one choose 20 distinct points — $K_1,\ldots,K_5, L_1,\ldots,L_5 \in OA$ and $M_1,\ldots,M_5, N_1,\ldots,N_5 \in OB$ — such that $K_iM_j = L_iN_j$ for all $1 \leq i,j \leq 5$?

Let $n$ be a positive integer with $\lfloor a\sqrt{10}\rfloor = n = \lfloor b\sqrt{11}\rfloor$ for some positive integers $a, b$. Prove there exists a positive integer $c$ with $n = \lfloor c(11\sqrt{10} - 10\sqrt{11})\rfloor$.

Let $m > k > 1$ be fixed positive integers. Find the greatest $N$ such that: one can place $N$ tokens in an $N \times N$ grid (one per row and column) with no horizontal and vertical gridlines splitting the grid into four rectangles where two non-adjacent ones have $\geq m$ and $\geq k$ tokens respectively.
Let $v \geq 4$ be a fixed positive integer. Find the smallest $e$ such that every connected graph on $v$ vertices with $e$ edges contains a cycle whose removal leaves the graph connected.

Acute $\triangle ABC$ with circumcenter $O$, orthocenter $H$. Line $OH$ meets $AB, AC$ at $B', C'$. Circles $(AB'C')$ and $(ABC)$ meet again at $S$. $K \in (ABC)$ with $AK$ tangent to $(AB'C')$. $M$ = second intersection of $AH$ with $(ABC)$. Prove $BC$, $SM$, $KH$ are concurrent.

Find all real polynomials $P$ for which there exist pairwise distinct nonconstant polynomials $f_1, f_2, f_3, f_4$ (positive leading coefficients) with $f_1 f_2 = f_3 f_4$ and $P(f_1)P(f_2) = P(f_3)P(f_4)$.
